subtasks.title: Build System, Branding, CI Pipeline & Browser Chrome Shell
subtasks.description:
Set up the complete Mogwser Firefox fork build infrastructure using Gluon, create custom branding, write platform-specific mozconfigs, configure GitHub Actions CI, and implement the custom browser chrome shell that replaces the default Firefox UI with Mogwser's sidebar-based layout.

Specific deliverables:
1. Initialize Gluon project with gluon.json configuration
2. Create branding directory (branding/mogwser/) with placeholder icons, app name 'Mogwser', identifiers
3. Write mozconfigs for linux-x86_64, macos-x86_64, macos-aarch64, windows-x86_64
4. Create package.json with npm scripts: init, build, build:ui, start, package
5. Write GitHub Actions CI workflow (.github/workflows/build.yml) that downloads Firefox, applies patches, builds, and runs tests
6. Write docs/BUILDING.md with build instructions for all 3 platforms
7. Create the browser.xhtml patch that loads Mogwser's chrome shell overlay
8. Implement MogwserShell.mjs — the top-level shell that initializes all subsystems
9. Create mogwser-shell.xhtml with the sidebar-based layout skeleton including insertion points for other modules (<!-- mogwser-tabs-slot -->, <!-- mogwser-splitview-slot -->, <!-- mogwser-sidepanel-slot -->)
10. Implement mogwser-shell.css with CSS custom properties at :root level for theming
11. Create prefs/mogwser.yaml with default preferences for all features
12. Write Mochitest browser chrome tests for shell initialization
subtasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. gluon.json is valid and references Mogwser branding
2. All 4 mozconfig files contain correct platform-specific compiler flags and branding reference
3. package.json scripts can orchestrate the full build lifecycle
4. GitHub Actions workflow is syntactically valid YAML with correct job dependencies
5. docs/BUILDING.md covers Linux, macOS, and Windows build steps
6. browser.xhtml patch cleanly adds Mogwser shell loading
7. MogwserShell.mjs initializes and exposes global singletons
8. mogwser-shell.xhtml has correct layout structure with labeled insertion points
9. CSS variables are defined at :root for --mogwser-sidebar-width, --mogwser-primary-color, --mogwser-secondary-color, --mogwser-accent-color, --mogwser-compact-mode, --mogwser-bg-opacity
10. prefs/mogwser.yaml contains preferences for all planned features
11. At least one browser chrome test verifies shell initialization

# Build System & Shell Agent

You are implementing the Mogwser Firefox fork build infrastructure and browser chrome shell.

## Project Context
Mogwser is an original Firefox fork achieving Zen Browser feature parity. This is a greenfield repo — you are creating all files from scratch. The repo currently has only an initial empty commit.

## Key Libraries & Tools
- **Gluon** (`gluon-build@next`): npm package for Firefox fork management. Install via npm. Handles Firefox source download, patch import/export, build orchestration. Config lives in `gluon.json`.
- **Firefox mach**: Mozilla's build system, invoked via `./mach build`, `./mach run`, `./mach test`
- **sccache**: Build cache, configured via `ac_add_options --with-ccache=sccache` in mozconfig

## Gluon Configuration (gluon.json)
The gluon.json file should specify:
- `name`: "Mogwser"
- `vendor`: "Mogwser"
- `appId`: "mogwser@mogwser.app"
- `binaryName`: "mogwser"
- `version`: object with `product` and `version` fields
- `buildTargets`: array of platform targets

## Mozconfig Conventions
Each mozconfig should include:
```
ac_add_options --with-branding=browser/branding/mogwser
ac_add_options --with-app-name=mogwser
ac_add_options --enable-application=browser
ac_add_options --disable-tests
ac_add_options --enable-optimize
mk_add_options MOZ_OBJDIR=@TOPSRCDIR@/obj-@CONFIG_GUESS@
```
Platform-specific flags:
- Linux: `-O3 -ftree-vectorize -msse3`, full LTO
- macOS x86_64: `-march=nehalem -mtune=haswell -O3`
- macOS aarch64: `-mcpu=apple-m1 -march=armv8.3-a+simd -O3`
- Windows: `-O3 -ftree-vectorize` with PGO support

## Branding Directory Structure
```
branding/mogwser/
├── configure.sh          # Branding variables (MOZ_APP_DISPLAYNAME, etc.)
├── branding.nsi          # Windows installer branding
├── pref/                 # Default preferences
│   └── firefox-branding.js
├── default16.png
├── default32.png
├── default48.png
├── default64.png
├── default128.png
├── content/
│   ├── about-logo.svg
│   └── about-logo@2x.png
└── locales/
    └── en-US/
        └── brand.properties
```

## Browser Chrome Shell Architecture
The shell replaces Firefox's default tab-on-top layout with a sidebar-based layout:
- The browser.xhtml patch adds a `<script>` tag to load MogwserShell.mjs
- MogwserShell.mjs is the entry point that initializes all subsystems in order
- mogwser-shell.xhtml defines the layout: `[sidebar (tabs + workspaces + sidepanel) | splitter | content-area (browser decks)]`
- Use `<!-- mogwser-tabs-slot -->`, `<!-- mogwser-workspace-slot -->`, `<!-- mogwser-splitview-slot -->`, `<!-- mogwser-sidepanel-slot -->` as insertion points

## CSS Variable Contract
Define these CSS custom properties at `:root` in mogwser-shell.css:
- `--mogwser-sidebar-width: 250px`
- `--mogwser-sidebar-collapsed-width: 48px`
- `--mogwser-primary-color: #4a90d9`
- `--mogwser-secondary-color: #2c3e50`
- `--mogwser-accent-color: #e74c3c`
- `--mogwser-bg-opacity: 1`
- `--mogwser-compact-mode: 0`
- `--mogwser-transition-speed: 0.2s`

## Preferences (prefs/mogwser.yaml)
Define defaults for:
- `mogwser.sidebar.width` (int, 250)
- `mogwser.sidebar.position` (string, "left")
- `mogwser.compact.enabled` (bool, false)
- `mogwser.compact.autohide` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.workspaces.enabled` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.splitview.enabled` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.splitview.min-panel-size` (int, 7)
- `mogwser.sidepanel.enabled` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.themes.gradient-enabled` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.privacy.tracking-protection` (bool, true)
- `mogwser.privacy.fingerprint-resistance` (bool, false)
- `mogwser.privacy.https-only` (bool, true)

## GitHub Actions CI
The workflow should:
1. Checkout code
2. Setup Node.js 21, Python 3, Rust
3. Install Gluon via npm
4. Run `npm run init` (download Firefox + bootstrap)
5. Run `npm run build`
6. Run `./mach test testing/mogwser/` (Mochitest)
7. Run `npm run package`
8. Upload artifacts

Use matrix strategy for linux, macos, windows.
Cache: Firefox source, sccache, node_modules.

## File Locations
All source files go under `src/mogwser/shell/`. Patches go under `patches/`. Branding under `branding/mogwser/`. Configs at root level.

## Conventions
- ES modules (.mjs) with chrome privilege
- Singleton pattern: export default class with static `init()` method
- Each subsystem exposes a global via `window.gMogwser<Name>`
- Use `Services.prefs` for all preference access
- Fire CustomEvents on `document` for cross-module communication
- CSS uses BEM-like naming: `.mogwser-shell__sidebar`, `.mogwser-shell__content`

## Testing
Write at least one Mochitest browser chrome test in `tests/browser/browser_mogwser_shell_init.js` that verifies:
- MogwserShell is loaded and initialized
- CSS variables are set on :root
- Sidebar element exists in the DOM

# Tab Management Agent

You are implementing the vertical tab bar, workspace system, and Firefox session patches for Mogwser.

## Project Context
Mogwser is an original Firefox fork. The repo is greenfield. Your files go under `src/mogwser/tabs/` and `src/mogwser/workspaces/`. Patches go under `patches/`.

Another agent is building the shell (`src/mogwser/shell/`) which provides insertion points:
- `<!-- mogwser-tabs-slot -->` — where your tab bar XUL/HTML gets injected
- `<!-- mogwser-workspace-slot -->` — where your workspace switcher gets injected

## Architecture

### Tab Bar
- `MogwserTabBar.mjs` is a singleton (window.gMogwserTabBar) initialized by the shell
- Renders tabs in a vertical list inside the sidebar
- Listens to Firefox's `TabOpen`, `TabClose`, `TabMove`, `TabAttrModified`, `TabSelect` events
- Each tab element: `<div class="mogwser-tab">` containing favicon img, title span, audio indicator button, close button
- Selected tab gets `.mogwser-tab--active` class
- Pinned tabs go in `.mogwser-tabs__pinned` section at the top

### Drag and Drop
- `MogwserTabDragDrop.mjs` handles HTML5 DnD events (dragstart, dragover, drop, dragend)
- On dragstart: set `dataTransfer` with tab index, add `.mogwser-tab--dragging` class
- On dragover: calculate drop position, show insertion indicator
- On drop: call `gBrowser.moveTabTo(tab, newIndex)` to actually move the tab
- Respect pinned/unpinned boundaries (can't drop unpinned into pinned section)

### Workspace System
- `MogwserWorkspaces.mjs` (window.gMogwserWorkspaces) manages workspace lifecycle
- Data model: `{ id: string, name: string, icon: string, theme: object|null, isDefault: bool }`
- In-memory cache: `Map<string, Workspace>`
- Tab assignment: each tab gets a `mogwser-workspace-id` attribute
- Switching workspace: iterate all tabs, set `hidden` attribute for non-matching workspace tabs
- Essential tabs: tabs with `mogwser-essential` attribute are never hidden
- Fire `MogwserWorkspaceChanged` CustomEvent on switch

### Workspace Storage
- `MogwserWorkspaceStorage.mjs` handles persistence to `mogwser-sessions.jsonlz4`
- Use Firefox's `IOUtils` and `Compression` APIs for LZ4 compressed JSON
- File location: profile directory, `mogwser-sessions.jsonlz4`
- Save on: workspace create/delete/rename, tab move between workspaces, browser shutdown
- Load on: browser startup, after session restore
- Data format:
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "workspaces": [
    { "id": "...", "name": "...", "icon": "...", "theme": null, "isDefault": true }
  ],
  "tabAssignments": {
    "<tabSyncId>": "<workspaceId>"
  }
}
```

### Firefox Patches

**tabbrowser-js.patch**: Modify `gBrowser.addTab()` to:
- Accept `mogwserWorkspaceId` in tab creation options
- Set `mogwser-workspace-id` attribute on new tabs
- Default to active workspace if not specified

**tabs-js.patch**: Modify the `allTabs` getter in `tabs.js` to:
- Add a `mogwserVisibleTabs` getter that filters by active workspace
- Modify drag-drop to respect workspace boundaries

**sessionstore.patch**: Modify `SessionStore.sys.mjs` to:
- Include `mogwser-workspace-id` and `mogwser-essential` in persisted tab attributes
- Fire `MogwserSessionRestored` event after session restore completes

## Conventions
- ES modules (.mjs) with chrome privilege
- Singleton pattern: `export default class MogwserTabBar { static init() { ... } }`
- Expose as `window.gMogwserTabBar`, `window.gMogwserWorkspaces`, etc.
- Use `Services.prefs.getBoolPref('mogwser.workspaces.enabled', true)` for feature checks
- CSS class naming: `.mogwser-tab`, `.mogwser-tab--active`, `.mogwser-tabs__pinned`
- Fire CustomEvents: `document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('MogwserWorkspaceChanged', { detail: { workspaceId } }))`

## Patch Format
Patches should be in unified diff format. Since we don't have the actual Firefox source, write patches as conceptual diffs with clear comments showing what's being modified and where. Use the format:
```
--- a/browser/base/content/tabbrowser.js
+++ b/browser/base/content/tabbrowser.js
@@ description of location @@
 context lines...
+added lines...
 context lines...
```

## Testing
- Browser chrome tests in `tests/browser/browser_mogwser_tabs.js` and `tests/browser/browser_mogwser_workspaces.js`
- xpcshell tests in `tests/unit/test_workspace_storage.js`
- Use `BrowserTestUtils` for tab operations in browser tests
- Test scenarios:
  - Tab bar renders correct number of tabs
  - Drag-and-drop reorders tabs
  - Pin/unpin moves tab to/from pinned section
  - Creating workspace adds it to switcher
  - Switching workspace hides/shows correct tabs
  - Essential tabs visible in all workspaces
  - Storage serialization round-trips correctly
  - Session restore preserves workspace assignments

subtasks.claudeMd:
# Advanced UI Agent

You are implementing split-view browsing, compact/expanded UI modes, and web side-panels for Mogwser.

## Project Context
Mogwser is an original Firefox fork. The repo is greenfield. Your files go under `src/mogwser/splitview/`, `src/mogwser/compact/`, and `src/mogwser/sidepanel/`.

Another agent is building the shell with insertion points:
- `<!-- mogwser-splitview-slot -->` — in the content area, where split-view overlay goes
- `<!-- mogwser-sidepanel-slot -->` — in the sidebar, where side-panel frame goes

The shell provides CSS variables you should use:
- `--mogwser-compact-mode`: 0 (expanded) or 1 (compact)
- `--mogwser-sidebar-width`: current sidebar width
- `--mogwser-sidebar-collapsed-width`: width in compact mode (48px)
- `--mogwser-transition-speed`: animation duration (0.2s)

## Split-View Architecture

### Binary Tree (SplitViewTree.mjs)
This is the core data structure. Implement two node types:

```javascript
class SplitLeafNode {
  constructor(tab) {
    this.tab = tab;           // Reference to MozTabbrowserTab
    this.parent = null;       // Reference to parent SplitNode
    this.sizeInParent = 50;   // Percentage (0-100) of parent space
  }
}

class SplitNode {
  constructor(direction) {
    this.direction = direction; // 'row' (horizontal) or 'column' (vertical)
    this.children = [];         // Array of SplitNode | SplitLeafNode
    this.parent = null;
  }
}
```

**Key operations:**
- `insertNode(existingLeaf, newTab, side)` — side is 'left'|'right'|'top'|'bottom'. Creates a new SplitNode parent if direction differs from current parent.
- `removeNode(leaf)` — removes leaf, collapses parent if only one child remains, redistributes space
- `swapNodes(leaf1, leaf2)` — exchanges positions in tree
- `calculatePositions(node, bounds)` — recursive. Returns `{top, right, bottom, left}` as percentages for CSS `inset` property
- `serialize()` / `deserialize()` — convert to/from JSON for persistence

**Position calculation algorithm:**
1. Root gets `{top: 0, right: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0}`
2. For each child of a row-direction node: left increases by cumulative sibling sizes, right = 100 - (left + sizeInParent)
3. For each child of a column-direction node: top increases by cumulative sibling sizes, bottom = 100 - (top + sizeInParent)

### Split View Manager (MogwserSplitView.mjs)
- Singleton: `window.gMogwserSplitView`
- Maintains array of split groups: `_groups = []`
- Each group has a root SplitNode and a set of tab references
- Maximum 4 tabs per group
- Creates splits via `splitTabs(tabs, direction)` or `splitIntoExisting(group, tab, side)`

**Panel rendering:**
- Each panel is a `<browser>` element (tab's browser) positioned absolutely within the content deck
- Set `is-mogwser-split="true"` attribute on the browser's container
- Apply CSS `inset` from calculated positions: `style.inset = \`${top}% ${right}% ${bottom}% ${left}%\``
- Create splitter handle `<div class="mogwser-split-handle">` between each pair of adjacent panels

**Resize logic:**
- On mousedown on splitter: record start position, identify the two adjacent leaf nodes
- On mousemove: calculate delta as percentage of container, adjust both nodes' sizeInParent (one increases, other decreases)
- Enforce minimum 7% (configurable via `mogwser.splitview.min-panel-size` pref)
- On mouseup: finalize, persist state
- Add `mogwser-split-resizing` attribute during resize to disable CSS transitions

**Session persistence:**
- Serialize split groups to JSON: `{ groups: [{ tree: serializedTree, tabIds: [...] }] }`
- Store in the shared `mogwser-sessions.jsonlz4` file (coordinate with workspace storage agent)
- Restore after `MogwserSessionRestored` event from session store

## Compact Mode Architecture

### MogwserCompactMode.mjs
- Singleton: `window.gMogwserCompactMode`
- Two states: expanded (default) and compact
- Toggle via `toggle()` method, keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+C
- Persisted via `mogwser.compact.enabled` pref

**Expanded mode:**
- Sidebar at full width (`--mogwser-sidebar-width`)
- Tab titles visible, workspace switcher visible
- Set `--mogwser-compact-mode: 0` on `:root`

**Compact mode:**
- Sidebar collapses to `--mogwser-sidebar-collapsed-width` (48px)
- Only favicons visible in tab bar
- Set `--mogwser-compact-mode: 1` on `:root`
- On hover: expand sidebar to full width temporarily (CSS transition)
- Set `mogwser-compact-hover` attribute on sidebar when hovered

**Auto-hide (optional, pref `mogwser.compact.autohide`):**
- Sidebar fully hidden until mouse approaches edge
- Show trigger zone (4px wide) at sidebar edge
- On mouse enter trigger zone: expand sidebar
- On mouse leave sidebar: collapse after 300ms delay

**CSS approach:**
```css
.mogwser-shell__sidebar[mogwser-compact] {
  width: var(--mogwser-sidebar-collapsed-width);
  transition: width var(--mogwser-transition-speed) ease;
}
.mogwser-shell__sidebar[mogwser-compact]:hover,
.mogwser-shell__sidebar[mogwser-compact-hover] {
  width: var(--mogwser-sidebar-width);
}
```

Fire `MogwserCompactModeChanged` CustomEvent with `{ detail: { compact: bool } }`.

## Web Side-Panel Architecture

### MogwserSidePanel.mjs
- Singleton: `window.gMogwserSidePanel`
- Renders a `<browser>` element (type="content") in the sidebar below the tab bar
- Loads arbitrary URLs specified by the user
- Panel persists across tab switches (it's independent of main content)

**UI components:**
- Panel container: `<div class="mogwser-sidepanel">`
- URL bar: `<input class="mogwser-sidepanel__urlbar">` for entering/changing URL
- Resize handle between side-panel and tab bar (vertical resize)
- Close button to dismiss panel
- Quick-access picker: list of pinned panel URLs (stored in prefs)

**Resize:**
- Side-panel height is adjustable via drag handle
- Minimum height: 100px
- Maximum: 70% of sidebar height
- Persist height in pref `mogwser.sidepanel.height`

**State persistence:**
- Current URL in `mogwser.sidepanel.url` pref
- Open/closed state in `mogwser.sidepanel.open` pref
- Pinned URLs in `mogwser.sidepanel.pinned` (JSON string pref)

## Conventions
- ES modules (.mjs) with chrome privilege
- Singleton pattern with static `init()` method
- Expose globals: `window.gMogwserSplitView`, `window.gMogwserCompactMode`, `window.gMogwserSidePanel`
- Use `Services.prefs` for preferences
- Fire CustomEvents on `document`
- CSS BEM naming: `.mogwser-splitview__handle`, `.mogwser-compact__trigger`

## Testing

**xpcshell tests** (`tests/unit/test_splitview_tree.js`):
- Tree insertion: add 2 tabs, verify correct structure
- Tree removal: remove a leaf, verify parent collapses
- Tree swap: exchange two leaves, verify positions
- Position calculation: verify inset values for known tree
- Serialization round-trip: serialize then deserialize, compare

**Browser chrome tests** (`tests/browser/browser_mogwser_splitview.js`):
- Create split with 2 tabs, verify both browsers visible
- Resize split, verify size changes
- Remove tab from split, verify remaining tab fills space

**Browser chrome tests** (`tests/browser/browser_mogwser_compact.js`):
- Toggle compact mode, verify sidebar width changes
- Verify hover expansion in compact mode

**Browser chrome tests** (`tests/browser/browser_mogwser_sidepanel.js`):
- Open side-panel with URL, verify browser loads
- Close and reopen, verify URL persistence

subtasks.title: Theme Engine & Privacy/Security Tooling
subtasks.description:
Implement the custom theme engine with gradient-based color schemes, color harmony algorithms, user-installable themes, and the privacy/security tooling panel with toggles for tracking protection, cookie management, fingerprint resistance, and HTTPS-only mode.

Specific deliverables:
1. Implement MogwserThemeEngine.mjs — global theme management, CSS variable injection, light/dark mode integration
2. Implement MogwserGradientPicker.mjs — HSL color wheel picker with dot-based color selection
3. Implement color harmony algorithms (complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, tetradic)
4. Implement per-workspace theme support (each workspace can have its own gradient)
5. Implement theme transition with double-buffer CSS technique (fade between old/new gradients)
6. Implement theme export/import as JSON
7. Implement user-installable theme directory with JSON manifest format
8. Create mogwser-themes.css with gradient background rendering and all theme CSS variables
9. Implement MogwserPrivacyPanel.mjs — unified privacy dashboard accessible from toolbar
10. Implement toggle switches for: Enhanced Tracking Protection, Cookie management (first-party isolation, third-party blocking), Fingerprint resistance, HTTPS-Only mode
11. Implement visual indicator in toolbar showing current protection level
12. Implement per-site exception management for privacy settings
13. Create mogwser-privacy.css
14. Write xpcshell unit tests for HSL conversion, color harmony calculations, theme serialization
15. Write Mochitest browser chrome tests for theme application and privacy panel toggles
subtasks.acceptance_criteria:
1. Theme engine applies custom color schemes via CSS variables at :root
2. Gradient picker allows selecting colors on HSL wheel and generates gradient themes
3. All 5 color harmony algorithms produce correct secondary/tertiary colors
4. Per-workspace themes apply when switching workspaces (listens for MogwserWorkspaceChanged event)
5. Theme transitions are smooth using double-buffer technique
6. Themes can be exported as JSON and imported back
7. User-installable themes load from a directory with JSON manifests
8. Light/dark mode respects prefers-color-scheme and adjusts theme accordingly
9. Privacy panel is accessible from toolbar button
10. All 4 privacy toggles correctly modify the corresponding Firefox preferences
11. Toolbar indicator reflects current protection level

# Themes & Privacy Agent

You are implementing the theme engine and privacy/security tooling for Mogwser.

## Project Context
Mogwser is an original Firefox fork. The repo is greenfield. Your files go under `src/mogwser/themes/` and `src/mogwser/privacy/`.

Other agents are building:
- Shell (provides CSS variable contract at `:root`)
- Workspaces (fires `MogwserWorkspaceChanged` event with workspace data including theme)

## Theme Engine Architecture

### MogwserThemeEngine.mjs
- Singleton: `window.gMogwserThemeEngine`
- Manages global theme state and per-workspace theme overrides
- Injects CSS custom properties on `:root` element
- Integrates with `prefers-color-scheme` media query

**Theme data model:**
```javascript
{
  id: string,
  name: string,
  type: 'gradient' | 'solid' | 'custom',
  colors: {
    primary: { h: number, s: number, l: number },
    secondary: { h: number, s: number, l: number },
    accent: { h: number, s: number, l: number },
    background: { h: number, s: number, l: number }
  },
  gradient: {
    angle: number,  // degrees
    stops: [{ color: string, position: number }]
  },
  darkMode: { /* same colors structure, adjusted for dark */ },
  metadata: { author: string, version: string }
}
```

**CSS variable injection:**
```javascript
applyTheme(theme) {
  const root = document.documentElement;
  const isDark = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches;
  const colors = isDark ? theme.darkMode : theme.colors;
  root.style.setProperty('--mogwser-primary-color', hslToString(colors.primary));
  root.style.setProperty('--mogwser-secondary-color', hslToString(colors.secondary));
  root.style.setProperty('--mogwser-accent-color', hslToString(colors.accent));
  root.style.setProperty('--mogwser-bg-color', hslToString(colors.background));
  // Apply gradient to background
  if (theme.gradient) {
    root.style.setProperty('--mogwser-gradient', buildGradientString(theme.gradient));
  }
}
```

**Double-buffer transitions:**
- Use `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements on the sidebar background
- `::before` holds old gradient, `::after` holds new gradient
- Transition: fade `::before` opacity from 1→0 over 0.2s while `::after` is already visible
- After transition completes, update `::before` to match `::after`

**Per-workspace themes:**
- Listen for `MogwserWorkspaceChanged` event
- Event detail includes `workspace.theme` (if set)
- If workspace has theme, apply it; otherwise apply global theme
- Cache computed CSS to avoid redundant style recalculation

### MogwserGradientPicker.mjs
The gradient picker is a UI component for choosing theme colors.

**HSL Color Wheel:**
- Render a circular canvas with hue mapped to angle, saturation to radius
- User places dots (draggable) on the wheel to select colors
- Convert pixel coordinates to HSL:
  - `hue = Math.atan2(y - centerY, x - centerX) * (180 / Math.PI) + 180` (0-360)
  - `saturation = distance / radius * 100` (0-100)
  - Lightness controlled by separate slider (0-100)

**Color Harmony Algorithms:**
All take a primary HSL color and return an array of complementary colors:

1. **Complementary**: `[(h + 180) % 360, s, l]`
2. **Analogous**: `[(h + 30) % 360, s, l]`, `[(h - 30 + 360) % 360, s, l]`
3. **Triadic**: `[(h + 120) % 360, s, l]`, `[(h + 240) % 360, s, l]`
4. **Split-complementary**: `[(h + 150) % 360, s, l]`, `[(h + 210) % 360, s, l]`
5. **Tetradic**: `[(h + 90) % 360, s, l]`, `[(h + 180) % 360, s, l]`, `[(h + 270) % 360, s, l]`

**HSL ↔ RGB conversion:**
Implement standard HSL to RGB and RGB to HSL functions. Also implement:
- `hslToString({h, s, l})` → `'hsl(h, s%, l%)'`
- `hslToHex({h, s, l})` → `'#rrggbb'`

### Theme Import/Export
- Export: serialize theme object to JSON, trigger file download
- Import: read JSON file, validate schema, apply theme
- User-installable themes: scan a directory (`<profile>/mogwser-themes/`) for `*.json` files
- Each theme file matches the theme data model above
- Theme manifest: the JSON file IS the manifest (includes metadata)
- Provide a "Themes" section in Mogwser settings listing installed themes

### Theme Preferences
- `mogwser.theme.active-id` (string): currently active theme ID
- `mogwser.theme.gradient` (string): JSON of current gradient config
- `mogwser.themes.gradient-enabled` (bool): whether gradient backgrounds are on
- `mogwser.theme.custom-colors` (string): JSON array of user-added custom colors

## Privacy Panel Architecture

### MogwserPrivacyPanel.mjs
- Singleton: `window.gMogwserPrivacyPanel`
- Renders a panel (popup) accessible from a toolbar button (shield icon)
- Panel shows current protection status and toggle switches

**Toolbar button:**
- Add via `CustomizableUI.createWidget()` with id `mogwser-privacy-button`
- Icon: shield SVG icon (create as inline SVG data URI)
- Badge shows protection level: green (strict), yellow (standard), red (disabled)
- Click opens the privacy panel popup

**Toggle switches — map directly to Firefox prefs:**

| UI Toggle | Firefox Preference | Default |
|-----------|-------------------|--------|
| Enhanced Tracking Protection | `privacy.trackingprotection.enabled` | true |
| Block Third-Party Cookies | `network.cookie.cookieBehavior` | 4 (reject trackers + partition) |
| First-Party Isolation | `privacy.firstparty.isolate` | false |
| Fingerprint Resistance | `privacy.resistFingerprinting` | false |
| HTTPS-Only Mode | `dom.security.https_only_mode` | true |

**Protection level calculation:**
```javascript
getProtectionLevel() {
  const tp = Services.prefs.getBoolPref('privacy.trackingprotection.enabled', false);
  const cookies = Services.prefs.getIntPref('network.cookie.cookieBehavior', 0);
  const fpi = Services.prefs.getBoolPref('privacy.firstparty.isolate', false);
  const rfp = Services.prefs.getBoolPref('privacy.resistFingerprinting', false);
  const https = Services.prefs.getBoolPref('dom.security.https_only_mode', false);
  
  const score = [tp, cookies >= 4, fpi, rfp, https].filter(Boolean).length;
  if (score >= 4) return 'strict';
  if (score >= 2) return 'standard';
  return 'minimal';
}
```

**Per-site exceptions:**
- Use Firefox's `SitePermissions` API or `PermissionManager` to manage per-site overrides
- UI: list of sites with exception toggles
- Add exception: enter URL, select which protections to disable for that site
- Remove exception: delete button next to each entry
- Store via `Services.perms.addFromPrincipal()`

**Panel layout (XUL/HTML):**
```
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ Mogwser Privacy Shield      │
│ Protection: ●●●○○ Standard  │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ ☑ Enhanced Tracking Protect │
│ ☑ Block Third-Party Cookies │
│ ☐ First-Party Isolation     │
│ ☐ Fingerprint Resistance    │
│ ☑ HTTPS-Only Mode           │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ Site Exceptions (3)     [+] │
│ example.com    [Remove]     │
│ bank.com       [Remove]     │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

## Conventions
- ES modules (.mjs) with chrome privilege
- Singleton pattern with static `init()` method
- Expose globals: `window.gMogwserThemeEngine`, `window.gMogwserGradientPicker`, `window.gMogwserPrivacyPanel`
- Use `Services.prefs` for all preference access
- Fire `MogwserThemeChanged` CustomEvent with `{ detail: { theme } }` when theme changes
- CSS BEM naming: `.mogwser-theme-picker__wheel`, `.mogwser-privacy__toggle`

## Testing

**xpcshell unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_theme_colors.js`):
- HSL to RGB conversion for known values (red=0,100,50 → 255,0,0)
- RGB to HSL conversion round-trip
- Complementary harmony: hue 0 → hue 180
- Analogous harmony: hue 120 → hues 150, 90
- Triadic harmony: hue 0 → hues 120, 240
- Theme serialization: create theme → export JSON → import → compare
- hslToHex for known values

**xpcshell unit tests** (`tests/unit/test_theme_serialization.js`):
- Theme export produces valid JSON matching schema
- Theme import rejects invalid JSON
- Theme import rejects JSON missing required fields

**Browser chrome tests** (`tests/browser/browser_mogwser_themes.js`):
- Apply theme, verify CSS variables are set on :root
- Switch to workspace with theme, verify theme changes
- Toggle dark mode, verify colors adjust

**Browser chrome tests** (`tests/browser/browser_mogwser_privacy.js`):
- Open privacy panel, verify all toggles render
- Toggle tracking protection, verify pref changes
- Check protection level badge updates
- Add per-site exception, verify it appears in list

# Integration Agent

You are merging work from 4 parallel agents into a cohesive Mogwser browser.

## Sub-branches to Merge
- `agent-task-ac7a69b7-sub-0`: Build system, branding, CI, browser chrome shell
- `agent-task-ac7a69b7-sub-1`: Vertical tabs, workspaces, session patches
- `agent-task-ac7a69b7-sub-2`: Split-view, compact mode, web side-panels
- `agent-task-ac7a69b7-sub-3`: Theme engine, privacy panel

## Merge Order
1. Start from `agent-task-ac7a69b7` (main task branch)
2. Merge sub-0 first (foundation — build system and shell)
3. Merge sub-1 (tabs and workspaces — depends on shell insertion points)
4. Merge sub-2 (advanced UI — depends on shell and workspace events)
5. Merge sub-3 last (themes and privacy — depends on shell CSS variables and workspace events)

## Conflict Resolution

### mogwser-shell.xhtml
Agent 0 creates this with insertion point comments. Agents 1-3 should NOT modify this file directly — they create their own component files. If any agent modified mogwser-shell.xhtml, keep Agent 0's version as base and manually add any needed references.

### MogwserShell.mjs
Agent 0 creates the initialization skeleton. After merging, update the init sequence to load ALL modules in correct order:
```javascript
static async init() {
  // 1. Theme engine first (others depend on CSS variables)
  await gMogwserThemeEngine.init();
  // 2. Tab bar (needs to exist before workspaces populate it)
  await gMogwserTabBar.init();
  // 3. Workspaces (assigns tabs to workspaces, triggers theme per workspace)
  await gMogwserWorkspaces.init();
  // 4. Split view (needs tabs and workspaces ready)
  await gMogwserSplitView.init();
  // 5. Compact mode (visual layer, can init independently)
  await gMogwserCompactMode.init();
  // 6. Side panel (independent sidebar feature)
  await gMogwserSidePanel.init();
  // 7. Privacy panel (independent toolbar feature)
  await gMogwserPrivacyPanel.init();
}
```

### mogwser-sessions.jsonlz4
Both workspaces (sub-1) and split-view (sub-2) write to this file. Ensure the storage format is:
```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "workspaces": { ... },
  "tabAssignments": { ... },
  "splitGroups": { ... }
}
```
If either agent used a different structure, normalize it.

### CSS Variables
Agent 0 defines base variables. Verify:
- Agent 2 (compact mode) uses `--mogwser-compact-mode`, `--mogwser-sidebar-width`, `--mogwser-sidebar-collapsed-width`
- Agent 3 (themes) uses `--mogwser-primary-color`, `--mogwser-secondary-color`, `--mogwser-accent-color`
- No naming conflicts between agents

### CustomEvents
Verify event name consistency:
- `MogwserWorkspaceChanged` — fired by workspaces (sub-1), consumed by themes (sub-3) and split-view (sub-2)
- `MogwserThemeChanged` — fired by themes (sub-3)
- `MogwserCompactModeChanged` — fired by compact mode (sub-2)
- `MogwserSessionRestored` — fired by session patch (sub-1), consumed by split-view (sub-2)

### prefs/mogwser.yaml
Agent 0 creates this with all preferences. If other agents added preferences in separate files or inline, consolidate everything into a single mogwser.yaml.

## Post-Merge Checklist
1. All files are in correct directories per project structure in PLAN.md
2. MogwserShell.mjs imports and initializes all 7+ modules
3. mogwser-shell.xhtml has all insertion point comments
4. All CSS files are imported/loaded by the shell
5. All event names match between producers and consumers
6. mogwser-sessions.jsonlz4 format is consistent
7. prefs/mogwser.yaml has all preferences from all modules
8. All test files exist and are syntactically valid
9. No duplicate preference names
10. No circular dependencies between modules

## Testing
After integration:
- Verify all test files parse (no syntax errors)
- Check that test expectations are consistent with final implementation
- Ensure test file paths match the project structure

After successful integration, create a single commit:
`feat: integrate all Mogwser modules — tabs, workspaces, split-view, themes, privacy`
